- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., sentiment > 0.30).  
- Underestimate prices during prolonged downward trends or when sentiment is negative (e.g., sentiment < 0.30).  
- Lag in correction: model often overshoots early in the forecast horizon, then gradually adjusts — correct by reducing later-period forecasts if sentiment is weak.  
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; apply dampening to forecasts when sentiment is volatile or near extremes.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish, then underestimating later periods when sentiment turns bearish.  
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is > 0.67, reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days; if sentiment < 0.20, increase forecast by 3–7% for the next 3–5 days.
